text:
jordan: Heads-up — noticed a cluster of tenant spikes from rapid reconnects this morning. Clients seem to retry aggressively and blow past per-minute quotas.

mira: ugh. links?

jordan: gist of logs: `client_id=acme-frontend` keeps reconnecting after an SSE 204 from proxy. Each reconnect counts as a new session and increments quota. snippet: 
```
[PROXY] 10:12:31 204 keepalive -> closed
[CLIENT] 10:12:31 reconnect
[PROXY] 10:12:31 new session -> quota +1
```

sam: is this the resume flow or full new session?

jordan: looks like full new session because resume token wasn't supplied. Maybe client drops token on 204.

kevin: Quick thought: we can either expand the implicit resume window on the server (treat short reconnects as resuming) or throttle rapid reconnects at the edge to protect quota accounting. Both have tradeoffs.

mira: expanding resume window fixes spikes but could mask real client rollovers. Also affects billing accuracy.

sam: throttle hurts latency-sensitive apps. They prefer a fast reconnect and get immediate results. If we delay, UX degrades.

jordan: telemetry hole: our console counts sessions by session-create events, but we don't tag them as "resume-implicit". Need a metric to differentiate. Without it, dashboard shows quota spikes and we push rollback panic.

kevin: Proposal: add `session.reason` tag: [new|resume|implicit-resume|throttle-suppressed] and bump console sample retention for these tags for a week during rollout.

mira: agree on tagging. For rollout UX: expose a toggle in console under Streaming -> Reconnect Handling: "Implicit resume grace (ms)" with default 2000, and "Reconnect soft-throttle" slider. That way devs can tune per-tenant.

sam: per-tenant knobs are nice but increases cognitive load. Could we do an adaptive policy: if client reconnect rate > X per minute then enable soft-throttle automatically and show alert?

jordan: adaptive is ideal. But we must be careful with canaries. We should ship as: 1) metric+tagging, 2) console visibility + per-tenant toggle (off by default), 3) adaptive pilot for high-reconnect tenants behind a feature flag.

kevin: implementation note: in proxy, check short gap (< grace_ms) and presence/absence of resume token. If absent but gap < grace_ms, mark `implicit-resume=true` and try to reuse KV cache session on the backend. If reuse fails, fall back to full new session and increment quota.

mira: we also need a clear UX in billing page: show estimated prevented duplicate charges due to implicit resume. Ops will love that.

sam: telemetry detail: we must instrument both counts (increment_attempts, prevented_duplicate_sessions) and SLOs (latency impact of soft-throttle). Add traces showing session lineage.

devops-bot: deploy candidate `resume-window-v2` to canary (eng-platform-canary) scheduled at 2026-04-02T18:00Z.

jordan: Nice. For the canary, let's enable tagging and console read-only toggle so we can watch without impacting defaults. Also add a guard in billing to only surface prevented duplicates after 24h aggregation to avoid churn.

kevin: one more edge: mobile clients on flaky networks may reopen TCP quickly but send stale resume token. We should accept stale tokens only if token_age < token_ttl and token_signature matches. Otherwise mark as new.

mira: agreed. I'll draft the console mockups and billing tooltip. Sam/kevin, can you PR the proxy changes with added metric tags?

sam: on it — will include test in `streaming_resume_test.go` for the 0-3s gap scenarios.

jordan: thanks. we'll reconvene after canary runs. :thumbsup:
